newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close higher in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close higher in sluggish trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed slightly higher on Monday in sluggish trade due to a lack of news, with declines in key blue chips offset by rises in Eletrobras and other power shares, brokers said.
"There's nothing to report today. It was slow," one dealer told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index closed just 0.06 percent higher at 66,492 points on trade totalling just 294 million reais.
Brokers said prices fluctuated mostly within a narrow range and trade was thin due to a lack of news and an absence of foreign players.

Benchmark Telebras preferred, which normally makes up about 60 percent of daily trade, seesawed throughout the day to close down 0.20 percent at 78.60 reais while its voting common share ended up a slight 0.07 percent.
Sao Paulo state bank Banespa, which jumped 18 percent in morning trade, pared gains to end flat at 4.80 reais after a wave of afternoon profit-taking.

The Banespa preferred has risen by more than 150 percent in the last eight sessions on expectations that a deal is close to being struck to turn the state bank into a federal one, as part of a renegotiation of state debts to the institution.
State miner Vale do Rio Doce preferred declined by 0.4 percent to close at 21.40 reais.
But despite declines in Vale and Telebras blue chips, other leaders posted enough gains to shore up the Bovespa index.
Petrobras, the state oil monopoly, saw its preferred share edge up 0.01 percent to 142.00 reais while state power firm Eletrobras preferred B rose 1.8 percent to end at 341.00 reais.
The rise in Eletrobras led the climb in other power firms.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) of nine most-liquid power stocks rose 0.26 percent to end at 1,796 points, boosted by strong earnings and privatization prospects for the sector.
